scientificScope: Initial individual author comparison of a credited artist interpretation. It remains unmeasured and partly stylized; software checks and author review are not independent biological validation.

rubric.identity: Species-level accepted linkage supported; photo and model are different individuals, not collection determinations.
rubric.body: Diagnostic broad head/trunk and shorter-tail cues present; exact proportions and tissues not measured.
rubric.surface: Continuous retained atlas; short-fur relief, marking scale and optics incomplete.
rubric.movement: Three bounded source studies only; complete gait, repose,feeding and physiology incomplete.

findings.shape: The aligned side/front/top views retain a broad-headed, muscular, shorter-tailed felid, rather than a recolored cheetah or leopard. Exact head/body ratios, shoulder volume, toe spacing and sexual/population differences remain unmeasured. Broad white paw tips and the muzzle look simplified relative to the selected living animal.
findings.surface: Original continuous UV atlas, material images, whisker geometry and skin weights retained. Rosettes with smaller internal spots are visible, with pale ventral regions. The atlas is an artist interpretation with repetitive-looking marking scale and flat short-fur relief; it is not a photograph-matched individual coat or measured optical surface.
findings.movement: Source clips were inspected at multiple phases. The original all-actions sequence contains standing, forepaw placement, stretching and self-cleaning, not a reviewed full walking cycle. Three bounded excerpts now stop before unrelated actions. Forepaw placement is explicitly not locomotion. Stretch entry/forelimb support/recovery and grooming paw-to-face movement were compared from three axes. Residual paw slip, precise fur contact, joint limits and forces remain unvalidated.
changes: Retained Ear.Rodriguez’s separately credited jaguar body, skeleton, skinning, images and UVs.
Corrected approximately30-degree creator-scene yaw using the head/pelvis axis; normalized display fit only. Side/front/top now align with the body instead of preserving an oblique source scene.
Separated and bounded original forepaw placement, stretch and grooming segments. Withdrew the draft walking claim after the actual screenshots showed a transition into stretching.
Added approximate posed-surface head, coat and forepaw landmarks with wider complete-region framing.
Rejected a field-drawing image and a habitat-only image as organism photographs; retained a visibly compatible living jaguar by Nicolas Olejnik with exact derivative/delivery checksums.
Preserved all305 previous species objects and all existing wolf/tiger surfaces.
remaining: A complete measured or independently reviewed walking/running gait is absent.
Supported resting/lying/sitting and physiological sleep remain incomplete; standing is not relabelled as rest.
Prey acquisition, carrying, manipulation, ingestion and jaw/prey contact require separate mechanisms. Grooming is not feeding.
Model proportions, claw sheaths, pads, fur, tissue strain and optics need expert measurements and further surface work.
No90percent accuracy score, independent specialist review, fitted biomechanics or research prediction is established.

sources.scope: Selected description and natural-history sections read: robust head/trunk, shorter limbs/tail and distinct rosettes. Not a specimen determination or measured fit.

sources.title: US Fish and Wildlife Service: Jaguar
sources.scope: Selected physical and behavioral account read. An agency species account, not a Smithsonian collection determination.

sources.title: Brunner et al. (2026): Feasts and fasts: feeding regimes and zoo-housed jaguar activity budgets
sources.scope: Full source PDF retrieved; methods context and actual Table 1 on printed p5 viewed. Three captive jaguars over eight weeks; behavioral labels are not measured kinematics or a wild activity schedule. No feeding/physiological result is reproduced by the model.

sources.scope: Official current species table checked for exact Panthera onca binomial. Population/subspecies concepts are not counted as separate archive species.

photograph.description: Authentic living jaguar photographed by Nicolas Olejnik, showing a muscular spotted trunk, broad head and stout forequarters amid vegetation. The animal is a different individual from the creator model.
